verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents creating CKS clusters through the Cloud Console, Terraform, or the API. Clusters run on bare-metal GPU nodes with InfiniBand networking, node pools can hold any number of nodes, and SUNK runs Slurm training jobs, so the multi-node, fast-interconnect training part is directly covered. The 'without a sales cycle' part is only partly shown: Spot and On-Demand capacity is pay-as-you-go with no long-term commitment, but quotas require requesting an increase for more capacity, and nothing documents self-serve signup. missing for 10: evidence of self-serve account signup and immediate large multi-node GPU quota without a sales or quota request, independent hands-on corroboration of provisioning and InfiniBand performance.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can provision a multi-node GPU cluster with fast interconnect for distributed training without a sales cycle

citations.quote: You can create a cluster with the Cloud Console or with Terraform.
CoreWeave Kubernetes Service runs your clusters directly on bare-metal GPU Nodes, with DPU isolation, per-cluster VPCs, and InfiniBand networking
You can deploy multiple Node Pools within a single cluster, where each Node Pool contains any number of Nodes.
Spot Node Pools provide pay-as-you-go access to high-performance bare-metal compute resources without long-term commitments or reservations.
Run training and inference workloads on the same cluster by running Slurm jobs inside Kubernetes.
